statement_text: I was closing up the store around 9:00 PM. I had just finished locking the back-room safe and was walking toward the front counter. Two men wearing black masks rushed in through the front door. The taller one, maybe 5 foot 10 or 5 foot 11, had a knife — a large kitchen-type knife with a black handle. He grabbed me by the collar and pushed me against the display case. He said 'Don't move or I'll cut you' in Hindi. His voice was deep and he spoke with what sounded like a western UP accent. The shorter one, maybe 5 foot 5, went straight to the center display case and started smashing the glass with a small hammer. I remember the glass shattering — it was incredibly loud, like a car crash. Shards flew everywhere and I felt some cut my left hand. They took about 15 to 20 gold necklaces and a tray of diamond rings from the center display, maybe worth 18 to 20 lakhs total. The whole thing lasted about 4 to 5 minutes. I was terrified — my heart was pounding so hard I thought I might collapse. The taller one kept looking at the door like he was nervous. Then they both ran out through the front door. I saw them get into a dark-colored SUV, it looked black or very dark blue, parked right outside the store. It drove off towards Pusa Road. I stumbled to the phone and called police at about 9:10 PM. My hands were shaking so badly I could barely dial. I don't understand why they targeted my shop — I'm just a small jeweller.

I run the textile shop right next to Mehta Jewellers. I was doing my end-of-day accounts at my desk near the back wall. Around 8:50 PM, I noticed through my window that a silver sedan, a medium-sized car, parked right in front of the jewelry store. I thought it was odd because that stretch is usually empty after 8:30 PM when the other shops close. The car sat there with its engine idling for maybe 10 minutes. Then around 9:00 PM I heard very loud crashing and banging sounds from next door — like glass breaking. I was scared but I went to my front door and opened it just a crack. I saw one man run out of Mehta Jewellers carrying a dark sports bag. He was medium height, maybe 5 foot 7, wearing all dark clothes and a mask or scarf over his face. He got into the silver car on the passenger side and it sped off immediately. It turned left and drove off towards Ajmal Khan Road, which is the opposite direction from Pusa Road. I only saw one man come out. I did not see a second person at all. After the car left I called Rajesh on his mobile to check if he was okay. He sounded very shaken.

I'm a security guard at the bank building across the street. I was standing near the ATM entrance on the first floor doing my regular round. Around 9:05 PM I heard a very loud noise from the direction of the jewelry shops. It sounded like shouting and glass breaking. I looked out and I could see through the glass front of Mehta Jewellers — there were two figures moving fast inside the store. One appeared to be behind the counter area. About two minutes later two men ran out of the store. Both wore dark clothes and masks. One was carrying what looked like a large bag or sack. They got into a dark-colored SUV, maybe black, parked right outside. The car took off very fast, heading toward Pusa Road. I immediately informed my supervisor and we called the police control room. I noted the time as 9:08 PM on my duty register.

I was nowhere near Karol Bagh that night. Me and my friend Deepak went to Sharma Dhaba in Rajouri Garden around 8:00 PM. We ordered butter chicken, dal makhani, and naan. I think I had two glasses of lassi. We were watching the cricket match on the TV there — India vs Australia. The match was very exciting, India was chasing 280 and it went to the last over. We stayed until about 10:30 PM when the dhaba was closing. Then Deepak dropped me home on his bike. I reached my house around 11:00 PM. I don't know anything about any robbery. I don't even know where Mehta Jewellers is. You can ask Deepak, he will confirm everything. You can also check the dhaba's CCTV if they have one.
